title: Lattice location of ion-implanted $^{6}\mathrm{He}$ in diamond
authors: U. Wahl, J. G. Correia, A. Costa, B. Biesmans, G. Magchiels, S. M. Tunhuma, A. Lamelas, A. Vantomme, and L. M. C. Pereira
abstract:
Author(s): U. Wahl, J. G. Correia, A. Costa, B. Biesmans, G. Magchiels, S. M. Tunhuma, A. Lamelas, A. Vantomme, and L. M. C. Pereira

Understanding the properties of helium in diamond is crucial for geological dating and possible quantum applications. Here, the authors determine the lattice location of ion-implanted short-lived 6He in single-crystal diamond at temperatures from 30°C to 800°C using the β− emission channeling technique. 6He preferentially occupies tetrahedral interstitial sites. From the temperature dependence of the interstitial fraction, the migration energy of He is estimated at 1.63–2.89 eV, implying unbound interstitial helium is unstable in diamond over geological timescales, an important insight to be considered in He-based dating methods.

title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
authors: G. Shankar and Joseph Maciejko
abstract:
Author(s): G. Shankar and Joseph Maciejko

The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem powerfully constrains the low-energy behavior of quantum many-body systems. In spin systems with spin rotation and conventional (Euclidean) lattice translation symmetries, it forbids a unique, gapped, symmetric ground state at half-odd-integer spin per unit cell. Here, the authors generalize this theorem to hyperbolic lattices — synthetic structures that emulate negatively curved space. Unlike Euclidean lattice translations, hyperbolic translations are noncommutative. By adapting a flux-threading argument, the authors derive LSM constraints on gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter.

title: Importance of nonlinear long-range electron-phonon interaction for the carrier mobility of anharmonic halide perovskites
authors: Matthew Houtput, Ingvar Zappacosta, William Wenborn, Serghei Klimin, Samuel Poncé, Jacques Tempere, and Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Houtput, Ingvar Zappacosta, William Wenborn, Serghei Klimin, Samuel Poncé, Jacques Tempere, and Cesare Franchini

The carrier mobility in many materials is dominated by scattering of the carriers with phonons. It is often calculated using only linear, one-electron–one-phonon interaction. Here, the authors present a first-principles calculation of the mobility including the nonlinear, long-range electron-phonon interaction, for the representative halide perovskite CsPbI3. It is shown that the temperature dependence of the carrier mobility decreases by about 10% due to the one-electron–two-phonon interaction, which is attributed to the strong anharmonicity and low phonon frequencies present in halide perovskites.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200301] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026

title: Many-body Euler topology
authors: Axel Fünfhaus, Titus Neupert, Thilo Kopp, and Roser Valentí
abstract:
Author(s): Axel Fünfhaus, Titus Neupert, Thilo Kopp, and Roser Valentí

The authors introduce here many-body Euler numbers as a counterpart to many-body Chern numbers to diagnose the spontaneous breaking of time reversal symmetry in (fractional) Chern insulators. In addition, a classification scheme to realize different topological phases in interacting systems using symmetry indicators is laid out.
